'''Anders C. Hansen''' is a Norwegian mathematician, who is currently a Professor of Mathematics at [[University of Cambridge]], where he is the head of the Applied Functional and Harmonic Analysis group, and also Professor II at the [[University of Oslo]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mn.uio.no/math/personer/vit/anderch/|title=Anders Hansen's homepage at the University of Oslo}}</ref> He works in [[functional analysis]], [[harmonic analysis]] (applied), [[foundations of mathematics]] (computational), [[data science]] and [[numerical analysis]] .<ref>{{Cite web |title=Anders Hansen – Applied Functional and Harmonic Analysis |url=http://www.damtp.cam.ac.uk/research/afha/anders/ |access-date=2024-01-16 |website=www.damtp.cam.ac.uk |language=en}}</ref>

==Education==
Hansen studied mathematics at the [[University of Cambridge]], [[University of California, Berkeley]] and the [[Norwegian University of Science and Technology]], where he was awarded a PhD (2008), a MA (2005) and a BA (2002) respectively.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.damtp.cam.ac.uk/research/afha/anders/CV_Short.pdf|title=CV}}</ref>

==Career and research==
He was a [[von Kármán]] instructor at [[California Institute of Technology]] from 2008 to 2009, held a junior [[research fellow]]ship at [[Homerton College, Cambridge]] from 2009 to 2012, and held a [[Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions]] fellowship at the [[University of Vienna]] in 2012. Since 2012, he has held a [[Royal Society University Research Fellowship]] (URF)<ref name=urfrs/> at the [[University of Cambridge]], where he is now a professor at the [[Faculty of Mathematics, University of Cambridge]] and a Bye-Fellow of [[Peterhouse]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pet.cam.ac.uk/master-fellows|title=Peterhouse Fellows}}</ref>

Among other results, he has established the Solvability Complexity Index (SCI) and its following classification hierarchy.<ref>{{cite journal|first=Anders C. |last=Hansen|title=On the Solvability Complexity Index, the n-pseudospectrum and approximations of spectra of operators|journal=[[Journal of the American Mathematical Society]]|volume=24|pages=81–124 |year=2011|doi=10.1090/S0894-0347-2010-00676-5 |doi-access=free}}</ref><ref name=Comp_Rend>{{cite journal|first1=J. |last1=Ben-Artzi| first2=A. C. |last2=Hansen|first3=O.|last3=Nevanlinna|first4=M. |last4=Seidel|title=New barriers in complexity theory: On the solvability complexity index and the towers of algorithms|journal=[[Comptes Rendus Mathematique]]|volume=535|pages= 931–936 |year=2015|issue=10 |doi=10.1016/j.crma.2015.08.002|bibcode=2015CRMat.353..931B |doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{cite arXiv |first1=J. |last1=Ben-Artzi| first2=M. |last2=Colbrook|first3=A. C.|last3=Hansen |first4=O. |last4=Nevanlinna |first5=M. C.|last5=Seidel |date=2020|title=Computing Spectra -- On the Solvability Complexity Index Hierarchy and Towers of Algorithms |class=cs.CC |eprint=1508.03280v5}}</ref><ref>{{cite arXiv |first1=A. |last1=Bastounis| first2=A. C. |last2=Hansen|first3=V.|last3=Vlacic |date=2021|title=The extended Smale's 9th problem – On computational barriers and paradoxes in estimation, regularisation, computer-assisted proofs and learning |class=math.OC |eprint=2110.15734v1}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Colbrook | first1=Matthew J. | last2=Antun | first2=Vegard | last3=Hansen | first3=Anders C. | title=The difficulty of computing stable and accurate neural networks: On the barriers of deep learning and Smale's 18th problem | journal=[[Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the USA]]  | volume=119 | issue=12 | date=2022-03-16 | article-number=e2107151119 | issn=0027-8424 | doi=10.1073/pnas.2107151119 | doi-access=free | pmid=35294283 | pmc=8944871 | bibcode=2022PNAS..11907151C }}</ref>
It is linked <ref name=Comp_Rend/> to [[Steve Smale]]'s question <ref>{{cite journal|author-link=Steve Smale|first=Steve|last=Smale|title= On the Efficiency of Algorithms in Analysis|journal=[[Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society]]|volume=13|pages=87–121|year=1985|issue=2 |doi=10.1090/S0273-0979-1985-15391-1|doi-access=free}}</ref> on the existence of iterative convergent algorithms for polynomial root finding answered by [[Curt McMullen]]<ref>{{cite journal|author-link=Curt McMullen|first=Curt|last=McMullen|title= Families of rational maps and iterative root-finding algorithms|journal=[[Annals of Mathematics]]|volume=125|pages=467–493|year=1987|issue=3 |doi=10.2307/1971408|jstor=1971408 |url=https://nrs.harvard.edu/urn-3:HUL.InstRepos:9876064 }}</ref><ref name=":0">{{cite journal|author-link2=Curt McMullen|first1=Peter|last1=Doyle |first2=Curt|last2=McMullen|title= Solving the quintic by iteration|journal=[[Acta Mathematica]]|volume=163|pages=151–180|year=1989|doi=10.1007/BF02392735|s2cid=14827783 |doi-access=free}}</ref> and [[Peter G. Doyle|Peter Doyle]],<ref name=":0" /> as well as [[Alan Turing]]'s work and the [[Arithmetical hierarchy]].

===Awards and honours===
In 2017, he was awarded the [[Leverhulme Prize]] for having "solved very hard problems and opened new directions in areas of great impact in applied analysis [...] Notably, by introducing the Solvability Complexity Index he has made a major contribution to the advancement of Smale's programme on the foundation of computational mathematics".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.leverhulme.ac.uk/philip-leverhulme-prizes-2017/ |title=Leverhulme Prize 2017 citations &#124; Leverhulme Trust }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.maths.cam.ac.uk/features/anders-hansen-finite-infinite |title=University of Cambridge Features: Faculty Insight}}</ref> In 2018, he was awarded the [[Institute for Mathematics and its Applications#Prize in Mathematics and its Applications|IMA Prize in Mathematics and its Applications]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ams.org/journals/notices/201906/rnoti-p942.pdf |title=Mathematics People &#124;Hansen Awarded 2018 IMA Prize &#124; Notices of the American Mathematical Society, Volume 66, Number 6}}</ref> for having "made a transformative impact on the mathematical sciences and their applications [...] in particular, for his development of the Solvability Complexity Index and its corresponding classification hierarchy".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ima.umn.edu/press-room/ima-prize-winner-2018 |title=Anders Hansen Awarded the 2018 IMA Prize in Mathematics and its Applications &#124; Institute for Mathematics and its Applications }}</ref> In 2019, he was awarded the [[Whitehead Prize]] of the [[London Mathematical Society]] for having "contributed fundamentally to the mathematics of data, sampling theory, computational harmonic analysis and compressed sensing" and "especially his development of the Solvability Complexity Index and its corresponding classification hierarchy 
".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.lms.ac.uk/sites/default/files/files/a_hansen.pdf|title=Whitehead Prize 2019 Citation for Dr Anders Hansen &#124; London Mathematical Society}}</ref>
